fatal_errors: The hypothesis addresses general alloy discovery rather than reducing the computational cost of faithful solid and liquid free-energy calculations.
It omits the central intervention: replacing liquid-phase EAM with an MTP and replacing thermodynamic integration with free-energy perturbation.
It provides no phase-free-energy framework retaining vibrational, anharmonic, electronic, and electron–vibration contributions.
The stated 1000–1600 K range, unspecified compositions, and generic initial state do not match TaVCrW at 0 GPa or the relevant approximately 2000–2400 K regime.
The baseline incorrectly compares alloy-processing routes rather than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
It predicts mechanical and corrosion properties instead of computational speed, phase-free-energy fidelity, melting temperature, and high-temperature thermodynamic observables.
The proposed falsification experiment cannot distinguish the requested computational hypothesis and incorrectly treats screening and modeling as processing methods.
The cited evidence does not establish FEP convergence from low-variance MTP–DFT energy differences, sub-meV-per-atom fidelity, or acceleration relative to TOR-TILD.
explanation: The response only shares the broad topic of high-entropy alloys and high-temperature behavior. It does not reconstruct or offer a technically relevant alternative to the target methodology. No MTP, FEP, DFT phase-space matching, solid/liquid free-energy comparison, electronic-excitation correction, SRO contribution, or quantitative speed/fidelity prediction is supplied. Its citations support generic high-throughput alloy design, phase stability, and classical-potential modeling, not the claimed solution to expensive fusion free energies. Generic limitations are mentioned, but they are unrelated to MTP training quality or applicability boundaries. The benchmark measures strength, hardness, and corrosion rather than solid and liquid Gibbs free energies, melting points, entropy terms, and agreement against TI or ab initio MD, so it cannot falsify the methodological claim posed by the query.
